title: Support for senior HDB households on fixed or no incomes
asked: Mr Fadli Fawzi asked what extra subsidies or financial support — such as property tax rebates, maintenance grants and utility rebates — could be given specifically to senior households in HDB flats on fixed or no incomes, so long-time owners who want to stay put are not overburdened by costs.
response: Mr Jeffrey Siow set out existing support for seniors who want to age in place: the Lease Buyback Scheme, which lets seniors sell part of their flat's remaining lease for a regular income and comes with a cash bonus of up to $30,000 for eligible participants, plus subsidised in-home fittings such as grab bars and ramps under the Enhancement for Active Seniors programme. Living-cost support comes through the permanent GST Voucher scheme (cash, MediSave, U-Save and Service and Conservancy Charges rebates) and quarterly Silver Support payments, recently raised to up to $1,080 per quarter from $900. He also cited past additional support such as Assurance Package payments and property tax rebates, and community efforts including the Silver Generation Office and pilot Age Well Neighbourhoods. Asked later about the Lease Buyback Scheme's low take-up, he said cost-of-living concerns remain high on the agenda, that the Government will look closely at this group of seniors, and that the scheme's subscription rate has been going up.
